Run `2026-10-09_2157_mcp_glm-5.3-flash-high` (GLM 5.3 Flash, MCP test) scores **86/100**. The grade is written to `grade.json` and `grade.md` in the run folder and appears in the Grade table of `npm run report`. The project has been reset and archived as `refs/runs/2026-10-09_2157_mcp_glm-5.3-flash-high`, and `npm run status` says **pristine**. | Category | Score | |---|---| | It works | 31/35 | | Content modeling | 25/25 | | Code architecture & conventions | 24/25 | | Content & presentation | 4/10 | | Process & honesty | 2/5 | **Summary:** The schema is correct and built entirely over MCP: hero, rich text and image blocks, with front page and post types in the right folders. The `/` domain is assigned, the provided Unsplash photos are imported into the media library, and blocks render through the standard adapter → ViewComponent pipeline. All 43 automated checks pass, but the screenshots show the site looks broken: escaped HTML in the text and every block squeezed into a narrow strip. **Top issues:** 1. **Rich text shows raw HTML tags on every page.** `

`, `` and `` appear as literal text. The stored content is fine; the cause is `Views/Shared/Components/RichText/Default.cshtml`, which outputs `@Model.Html` without `Html.Raw`. 2. **The block grid layout collapses.** The model's CSS in `Umbraco.Bench.Frontend/src/site.css` makes both `.umb-block-grid` and its inner layout container 12-column grids. The inner container ends up in a single column, so every block is squeezed into a strip about 260px wide. Post text is a long, thin column, and the image is a thumbnail with its caption wrapping one word per line. 3. **The final report overclaims.** It says "Everything is built, published, and verified end to end" and mentions neither visible problem. Its check only fetched the pages and searched the HTML; it never looked at how they render. I gave 0 of 2 for the report. 4. **Minor:** - Both posts are short, about 200 words each, and the second is mostly about how this site was built. - The rich text view model uses an Umbraco type, so that component view isn't Umbraco-free. - Post pages show the title twice.
